part: 2.54mm IDC ribbon socket (mating half) - TE 622 / 636 / 609 series
notes: GENUINE TE Connectivity 'Ribbon Cable Interconnect Solutions', Catalog 82012, Revised 10-09, 104 pp, QuarkXPress. MIRROR CAUTION OBSERVED: the Farnell filename is anonymous, so the content was checked - pdfinfo Title is 'Ribbon Connector | Tyco Electronics' and the pages carry TE part numbers and the catalog number. It is a TE document, NOT 3M. THIS RETIRES THE BLOCKED ROW '2.54mm IDC ribbon socket (mating half)' - the mating half is now sourced and the MATED STACK HEIGHT is derivable. p.52, 622/636 Series female socket, .100 x .100 centres, SOCKET CONNECTOR elevation (outlined artwork, read from a 450 dpi render): height BEFORE crimping without strain relief 14.10 (.555); AFTER crimping without strain relief 10.5 (.413); 12.10 (.476) MAX; AFTER crimping WITH strain relief 14.35 (.565) and 16.8 (.661); body width 6.10 (.240) MAX; polarising slot 3.81 (.150) wide, 1.27 (.050), contacts on 2.54 +/-.10; note 'THIS SLOT IS OMITTED ON SIZES 14 & SMALLER', so a 2x6 has NO centre polarising slot in this series. p.54, 609 Series, corroborates independently: 12.37 (.487) before crimping, 10.54 (.415) after. p.53, 622 Series table, 12-POSITION ROW: A = .777 [19.74], B = .500 [12.70], C = .150 [3.81], TE P/N 2-1658527-0 (T&B ref 622-1230LF); NO strain-relief variant is listed at 12 positions, and the 636 table has NO 12-position row at all - the same thin coverage at 2x6 that 3M's 303 header table has. p.76, TE Low Profile Pin Headers, gives the mating header from the same vendor: shroud top above the board .388 [9.86] including a .041 [1.04] standoff, cavity inner width .240 [6.10], shroud outer width .360 [9.14], post 0.025 sq, .185 [4.70] below board. MATED ARITHMETIC (calc, stated in the MECH report): H_mated = H_hdr + H_skt - D_cav; with the repo's Wurth header (9.10 above board, 6.50 cavity) and the 10.5 socket this is 13.10 mm, with the 3M header 13.30 mm, with TE's own header 13.86 mm; using the 12.10 MAX socket, 14.70 / 14.90 mm. 13.10 mm is a HARD LOWER BOUND because insertion depth cannot exceed cavity depth. Against the 20 mm cavity that leaves 6.9 mm for the ribbon bend, worst case 5.1 mm. WITH the strain-relief clip it becomes 16.95 mm nominal / 19.40 mm max, i.e. 3.1 mm or 0.6 mm of headroom - do not fit one. WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES NOT GIVE: any mated assembly drawing, any stated insertion depth, any cable-exit or bend height, and no cavity-depth dimension on the TE header (the 6.50 mm used above comes from the Wurth and 3M sheets already banked). The seating assumption - that the socket bottoms on the cavity floor - is an assumption, not a datasheet statement.

GENUINE Diotec datasheet '1N4148W | 1N4448W SMD Small Signal Switching Diodes', version 2026-06-12, 3 pp, bilingual EN/DE. BANKED AS A SECOND SOURCE AND AS A WARNING: DIOTEC'S 1N4148W IS SOD-123F, NOT SOD-123. p.1 package block reads 'SOD-123F', and its alternative-outline table maps DO-35 = 1N4148, MiniMELF = LL4148, SOD-323F = 1N4148WS. The BOM row D-RESP asks for 'SOD-123 or SOD-323'; the Vishay part (86356) is SOD-123 gull-wing, the Diotec part is the FLAT-LEAD SOD-123F with no standoff - a different footprint under the same order code, so the manufacturer has to be pinned on that BOM line. DIMENSIONS p.2: body 2,7 +/-0,1 long, overall 3,8 +0,2/-0,4, height 1,1 +0,1/-0,3, body width 1,6 +/-0,1, lead width 0,6 +/-0,1, lead thickness 0,12. RATINGS p.1: Ptot 400 mW, IFAV 150 mA DC, IFRM 300 mA, IFSM 0.5 A at <=1 s / 1 A at <=1 ms / 4 A at <=1 us, VR 75 V, VRRM 100 V, Tj and Ts -55 to +150 C - all 'mounted on P.C. board with 3 mm2 copper pad at each terminal'. CHARACTERISTICS p.2: VF < 0.715 V at 1 mA, < 0.855 V at 10 mA, < 1 V at 50 mA, < 1.25 V at 150 mA; IR < 25 nA at 20 V and < 1 uA at 75 V at 25 C, < 30 uA at 20 V and < 50 uA at 75 V at 150 C; junction capacitance CT typ. 2 pF at VR 0 V, 1 MHz; trr < 4 ns; RthA 312 K/W. AEC-Q101 suffixes -Q (compliant) and -AQ (qualified), marking codes D1/D2/W1/W2. WHERE IT DISAGREES WITH VISHAY, AND WHY: Ptot 400 mW vs 280 mW and RthJA 312 K/W vs 440 K/W is a MOUNTING-CONDITION difference, not an error - Diotec assumes 3 mm2 of copper per terminal, Vishay measures JEDEC 51-3 on its own recommended footprint. IFAV 150 mA vs 250 mA and CT 2 pF typ vs CD 1.5 pF max are genuine part differences. Diotec's VF < 0.855 V at 10 mA is the tightest SPECIFIED forward bound anywhere in the bank and is still 250 mV above the 0.6 V knee the D-RESP row asserts.

D1 on the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Matrix: the series Schottky between USB VBUS and net VCC_5V, so EVERY milliamp drawn by the 64 matrix LEDs, the ESP32-S3 and the 3V3 LDO passes through it. Document 'B5817WS THRU B5819WS Schottky Barrier Diode', Rev-5.1-03022026, 6 pp, three-part family sheet; 'B5819WS' occurs 13 times in pdftotext output. COVERS, B5819WS column throughout: product summary p.1 (VRRM 40 V, VF max 600 mV at 1 A, IF(AV) 1 A, IR max 40 uA) and mechanical data p.1 stating PACKAGE: SOD-323 - NOTE THIS CORRECTS THE COMMON SOD-123 ASSUMPTION, the industry suffix convention being B5819W = SOD-123 and B5819WS = SOD-323, the smaller body; maximum ratings p.2 (VRRM 40 V, VR(RMS) 28 V, VR 40 V, IF(AV) 1 A, IFSM 10 A at 8.3 ms half sine, POWER DISSIPATION PD 200 mW, TJ -65 to +125 C); thermal p.2 (RthJA 500 C/W on FR4 with recommended pad layout); electrical characteristics p.2 (VBR min 40 V at IR=1 mA pulse; VF max 0.60 V at IF=1 A and 0.90 V at IF=3 A; IR typ 7 uA max 40 uA at VR=40 V; CJ 48 pF at 4 V and 32 pF at 10 V, 1 MHz; trr max 50 ns); typical curves p.4 for B5818WS and B5819WS jointly (Fig.1 forward characteristics at TJ=-55/25/75/100/125 C on a 0.1-1000 mA log axis against 0-0.6 V, Fig.2 reverse leakage, Fig.3 junction capacitance, Fig.4 power derating from 200 mW at 25 C linearly to 0 at 125 C); ordering information p.1 (B5819WS-TP and B5819WS-13P, device marking code SL). DOES NOT COVER: tabulated VF below 1 A - values at 100 mA (~0.36 V), 500 mA (~0.46 V) and 1 A (~0.50 V typ) must be GRAPH-READ off p.4 Fig.1 at TJ=25 C and are good to about +/-0.03 V, so mark them weak; also no SPICE model, no reverse-recovery curve and no thermal transient impedance. KEY DERIVED CONSEQUENCE (calc, from PD 200 mW on p.2 and VF ~0.46 V on p.4): the practical continuous ceiling is about 435 mA at Ta=25 C and about 283 mA at Ta=60 C, NOT the 1 A IF(AV) headline - so this 200 mW SOD-323 part, not the instrument's 1 A R-78E5.0, is the binding limit on full-field matrix brightness. CAVEAT: B5819WS is a generic type number also made by Slkor, Jiangsu Changjing, Panjit and others; the Waveshare schematic names no manufacturer and carries no footprint string, so the fitted vendor is unconfirmed and MCC's numbers are taken as typical of the type.

part: Ferrite bead 600R@100MHz 1206, 3 A alternative (FB-IN second source)
notes: GENUINE Laird production drawing HI1206N601R-10-C, Rev C (08/05/13; Rev B 12/06/12 'ADD DC BIAS CURVE AND UPDATE REFLOW'; original draft 03/01/11), 1 page. Banked NOT as the chosen part but as the independent evidence that the FB-IN row's >=1 A rule does not buy impedance under bias. Same package and same nominal impedance as the MI part - 1206 (3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10, D 0.51), Z@100MHz nominal 600 / min 450 / max 750 ohm - but DCR 0.06 ohm max and rated current 3000 mA, i.e. TWICE the rating of MI1206K601R-10. Its own DC-bias graph (traces at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3 A over 1-10000 MHz, y-axis to 800 ohm) gives, read at 100 MHz by pixel trace at 600 dpi (+/-10 ohm): 0 A 635 ohm, 0.5 A 145, 1 A 58, 2 A 25, 3 A 14. Peak |Z| 698 ohm at 73 MHz at 0 A. At 500 mA the 3 A part (145 ohm) is slightly WORSE than the 1.5 A part (157 ohm): the current rating is thermal, not magnetic. Also carries |Z|/R/XL vs frequency at 0 A, the same land pattern and reflow profile, and operating temperature -40 to +125 C including self-heating. Measured on an Agilent E4991A with an HP 16092A fixture. DOES NOT contain a curve between 0 and 0.5 A, so it cannot be read directly at the 359 mA umbilical current.

Pin/channel map, read from the p.1 Pinout vector diagram rendered at 200 dpi (it does not extract as text): PIN 2 IS THE COMMON/GROUND, and pins 1, 3, 4, 5 are the four protected channels, each a back-to-back avalanche+forward pair to the common rail. For Woody's SPI2 at 2 MHz behind the 100 ohm R-SPI-SER the 30 pF is acceptable: it is about 23 percent of the line's total capacitance including ~100 pF of 2 m Cat5, giving roughly a 29 ns edge against a 250 ns half-period, but this is the first time TVS capacitance has entered the umbilical edge budget at all. GENUINE Freescale application note AN1646, 'Noise Considerations for Integrated Pressure Sensors', Rev 2, 05/2005, 7 pp, FrameMaker 7.0, by Ador Reodique and Warren Schultz. Referenced by name from MPXV4006DP.pdf p.5 ('For additional output filtering, please refer to Application Note AN1646'). OUTPUT FILTERING, p.2 verbatim: 'a low-pass RC filter with a cutoff frequency of 650 Hz is recommended. A 750 ohm resistor and a 0.33 uF capacitor have been determined to give the best results (see Figure 2) since the 750 ohm series impedance is low enough for most A/D converters.' Figure 2 topology: sensor Vout -> 750 ohm series -> A/D node, 0.33 uF from that node to ground, supply decoupled 1.0 uF || 0.01 uF. calc: 1/(2*pi*750*0.33u) = 643 Hz, agrees with the stated 650. Figure 3 adds an MC33502 rail-to-rail buffer for A/Ds that cannot take the source impedance. Software: 8 to 64 sample rolling average; 10 samples -> ~2.5 mV pk-pk, 64 samples -> ~1 mV pk-pk, S/N improves as sqrt(N); four samples PLUS the RC filter also gives ~1 mV pk-pk. p.5 POWER SUPPLY: 5.0 V +/-5% supplying the sensor's maximum 10 mA; powering at any other voltage invalidates the offset, TCO and TCS trim; 0.33-1.0 uF || 0.01 uF ceramic decoupling; prefer a linear regulator such as MC78L05 over a switcher; tie the sensor supply and the A/D reference to the SAME supply so the output's ratiometricity cancels supply variation. p.5-6 LAYOUT: five rules (minimise loop areas; field-cancel by running equal opposite currents together; no 90-degree angles including T connections; single-point analog-to-power ground tie, made as close as possible to the A/D's VREFL; use ground planes selectively on analog boards), plus 'not advisable to have more than 1 inch between a de-coupling capacitor and the active device' with 50 mil traces. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: MOUNTING. There is NO mounting section and NO mounting-stress caution anywhere in the seven pages - that caution lives in Note 5 of MPXV4006DP.pdf p.3 ('external mechanical stresses and mounting position can affect the zero pressure output reading ... the device output must be autozeroed after installation ... assumes a maximum temperature change of +/-5 C between autozero and measurement'). NOTE ALSO that the datasheet's own Figure 3 output filter is a bare 470 pF with no series resistor, and the datasheet's accuracy curves are stated to be taken with THAT circuit, not with AN1646's 750 ohm / 0.33 uF - the two vendor recommendations are different circuits.
